thread:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: `PD-4972` fired for `inference-dedicated-queue` - high queue depth and 5xx spike. Escalation level: automatic -> on-call.
Alex H.: ACKing, on call. looking now. timezone: PST.
Maya G.: i'm on call too, will correlate with recent deploys. any customer impact known?
Jenna: seeing errors in downstream router (502/504) and latency spiking. quick check: redis queue length is high.
Samir: pinging metrics: request_rate steady, but processing throughput dropped ~60% last 6m. KV cache hit ratio unchanged.
Alex H.: running quick healthcheck
Alex H.: ``curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}\n' https://inference-api.prod/v1/health`` -> 502 0.23
Maya G.: logs show many `ExecutorTimeoutError` on worker pods. tail:
```
2026-03-14T09:12:01Z worker-12 inference_executor.py Timeout after 30s waiting for model chunk
2026-03-14T09:12:02Z worker-12 kvcache.py Eviction triggered - hot keys: user:embed
```
Samir: looks like a hotkey + straggler workers issue. Could be a bad batch size change or quantized kernel regression from last deploy at 09:00.
Jenna: deployment at 09:00 was `dedicated-runtime v3.4.1` -> changed NATIVE_BATCH_TIMEOUT from 25->40ms per canary notes.
Maya G.: that config should reduce latency, not increase timeouts. suspect fallback to slower kernel on some GPU nodes. checking node GPUs now.
Plato Ops: forwarding: incident runbook says first action: isolate affected pool and route traffic to standby pool. want me to flip routing for canary shard?
Alex H.: +1, prepare rollback of routing. Jenna, can you open a temporary route to dedicated-fallback pool and drain affected pods?
Jenna: doing it now. command:
```
# add route to fallback pool
redwood route update --model inference-embed --pool dedicated-fallback --weight 0.4
# start draining
kubectl annotate pods -n inference worker-12 sample-drain=true
```
Jenna: route update applied, weight 0.4. starting to observe traffic shift.
Maya G.: monitoring: 30s after shift, queue depth trending down. 5xx rate reducing from 6% -> 2%.
Samir: still seeing a small % of requests hitting affected pods via sticky sessions. adding IP-based deny on affected worker nodes.
Alex H.: granted. make sure we have rollback plan. also posting customer impact: partial degradation for % of requests to embeddings/generate endpoints in EU region (~short window).
Maya G.: estimated customer impact: ~12% requests saw >2s tail latency; ~3% saw 5xx. Affected customers: high-QPS partners using embeddings batch API. opening customer-impact ticket.
Plato Ops: should we escalate to Dedicated infra team? Likely root cause is kernel fallback on mixed GPU types - need kernel pinning.
Alex H.: yes escalate. @Plato Ops please claim PD-4972 for escalation to infra. I'll stay primary for mitigation and handoff when stable.
Plato Ops: claiming PD-4972 for infra escalation. pinging infra on-call.
Incident Bot: PD-4972 acknowledged by Alex H. at 2026-03-14T09:14:05Z. Escalation to infra assigned to Plato Ops.
Jenna: we've drained and restarted 6 affected pods. healthchecks now: 200 OK. still see small backlog clearing.
Maya G.: running a quick script to replay failed requests for customers in a safe queue to check output consistency.
Alex H.: good, ensure we don't double-charge tokens. route replay to staging compute.
Samir: while draining, I noticed one node had mismatched CUDA runtime (nv 12.5 vs 12.4) and the fallback kernel log correlates. raising a config drift alert.
Plato Ops: infra on-call replied: will patch node CUDA to 12.4 and force kernel consistency across pool. ETA 25m for rolling patch.
Jenna: reducing route weight to fallback to 0.2 to limit capacity there while patching.
Maya G.: metrics update: 5xx now down to 0.6%, queue depth nearly normal. customer impact window estimated ~09:10-09:30 UTC.
Alex H.: creating incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-7833 and linking PD-4972. Notes: temporary routing change, drained pods, infra patch scheduled.
Samir: adding a quick mitigation note for runbook: if kernel fallback detected, auto-route 30% to dedicated-fallback and alert infra-runner.
Plato Ops: acknowledged, will follow up with infra post-patch checklist. also requested node image bake to avoid future drift.
Jenna: confirming we should keep the routing change for 1h and revert if stable. anyone object?
Maya G.: fine with 1h, but add canary traffic check before full revert.
Alex H.: agreed. I'm going to handoff primary after 20m to Plato Ops for verification and postmortem. final status update in 15.
Incident Bot: PD-4972 status: mitigated -> partial mitigation in place. next reminder in 15m.
(12 minutes later)
Plato Ops: infra patch completed on 3/4 nodes; final node draining in progress. kernel mismatch resolved on patched nodes.
Maya G.: no new 5xx spikes in last 8m. latency back to baseline.
Alex H.: handing primary to Plato Ops now. leaving note: root cause likely kernel fallback on a subset of mixed-version GPU nodes causing increased exec latency and queue buildup. Steps taken: route shift, pod drain/restart, patch nodes, open INF-7833.
Plato Ops: taking over. will run the convergence checks and then start postmortem.
Jenna: customer comms draft: "We experienced a brief service degradation affecting a subset of inference requests between 09:10-09:30 UTC. The issue is mitigated and we are investigating root cause; no data loss." ping to Growth/Sales for notification?
Samir: tagging Growth: @growth-team FYI; also attaching logs and rough timeline to INF-7833.
Plato Ops: will follow up with a timeline and action items. closing PD-4972 once we confirm all nodes patched and routing restored.
Incident Bot: PD-4972 resolved by Plato Ops at 2026-03-14T09:44:59Z. Resolution summary posted to INF-7833.
Alex H.: thanks everyone. quick retro: add node image drift checks to pre-deploy and add an auto-fallback throttle for routing changes.
Maya G.: agreed. I'll file two follow-ups: one for runbook update, one for pre-deploy node-check job.
Jenna: adding a postmortem meeting invite for 2026-03-16 10:00 UTC.
Plato Ops: marking this thread closed on my side. good job team :thumbsup:
